title: Metric dictionary completeness: all 32 section-20 metrics have owner, unit, window and exclusions
risk: A metric is quoted in a gate or an investor document that the dictionary never defined, so numerator, denominator and window are decided per report and two teams publish two different numbers under one name.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
The dictionary is loaded read-only together with the section-20 metric list; the case may not add, rename or merge a metric.
A metric without a covering case is treated as a coverage gap that is reported, not as an empty dashboard cell.

steps.action: Load the section-20 metric list and the platform dictionary
steps.expected: The list holds 32 names in 5 groups with the counts 7 marketing, 7 sales, 6 customer care, 5 customer success and 7 AI system.

steps.action: Match every dictionary entry against the list
steps.expected: Each of the 32 names resolves to exactly one entry and every entry declares owner, unit, numerator, denominator, window and exclusion rule.

steps.action: Attempt to register a metric that is not in section 20
steps.expected: The registration is refused; the dictionary holds no orphan metric and an additional metric stays a labelled extension that cannot be published as an SRS KPI.

steps.action: Attempt to compute a metric whose entry is missing its denominator
steps.expected: Publication is blocked and the gap is reported, instead of defaulting the denominator to the row count of the whole table.

assertions: All 32 section-20 metric names resolve to exactly one dictionary entry each, with per-group counts 7/7/6/5/7 and no duplicate name.
Every entry declares the fields required to reproduce the value; a missing field blocks publication rather than defaulting to a plausible substitute.
No metric outside section 20 is published as an SRS KPI, and an extension metric is visibly labelled as an extension.
The reverse map is available: each metric names the cases that cover it, so an uncovered metric appears as a reported gap.
forbidden: Publishing a metric that has no dictionary entry.
Renaming or merging a section-20 metric to fit an existing entry.
Silently defaulting a missing numerator or denominator.
evidence: Dictionary dump with the 32 entries and all declared fields.
Coverage gap report listing metrics with no covering case (expected to be empty).
cleanup: Delete gov- dictionary snapshot rows after export.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
prerequisites: ASM-002 targets are not locked, so the dictionary carries definitions, units and windows only; no target figure is part of the dictionary.
